notes_for_editor: Source conflicts, all flagged in the story where they matter: first lighting 15 Oct 1857 (museum) vs 12 Oct (LF); tower height 58 ft (museum), 55 ft (LF), 35 ft base-to-lantern (USLHS), about 18 m (Wikipedia, lead only); focal height 110 ft (museum, LF) vs 103 ft (USLHS, used in the record); 1853 letter writer: 'Master of the steamer Bay State' (museum) vs 'a local ship captain' (LF); Stella Maria Prince's acting term June 1903-November 1904 (museum, USLHS 1903-1904) vs 'a few months' (LF); George Ehrhardt's service to 1933 (USLHS) vs commuting to Shinnecock until 1935 (museum); skeleton tower 50 ft (museum) vs 40 ft (LF); property: $1 purchase (museum) vs lease 1933 and conveyance 1937 (LF), Wikipedia's January 1934 $1 purchase not used; wartime occupant: military (museum) vs Civilian Defense Corps (LF); original lens: third order lost (museum), while LF describes a fourth-order lens now displayed in the museum. LF says 'only nine head keepers'; the archive lists eight principal keepers plus Stella Maria Prince as acting. Keepers matched by the USLHS roster (roster.py, person slugs on every line). Daniel Goldsmith's 1877-1881 first-assistant line: LF calls him 'Daniel Goldsmith, Jr.', but the archive lists one person slug for both stints; kept as printed. The archive roster lists 21 lines, all copied. No other-station links were added: LF says Robert Ebbitts came from Cedar Point Lighthouse, but no dates for that service are sourced, so no other_stations entry was made. The 1896 entry is confirmed at scan page 316 with corpus.py page (the OCR line reads '277. Horton Point, X. Y.'; the repair list was read from OCR text, not the page image). The 1922 entry is confirmed at printed p. 47 (scan page 747), and its table heading reads 'COMPLETED DURING FISCAL YEAR 1922'. The 1922 line sits in the Third District list in the report of the Commissioner of Lighthouses. The NRHP nomination PDF (npgallery 94001237) is a 'not yet digitized' placeholder; only the NPGallery asset record was used. Newspapers: two Chronicling America searches for Horton Point (1895-1897, 1896 keepers) and a 1903 Ebbitts search returned no readable hits about the station; none is used. Riverhead County Review (27 July 1933) is cited only as quoted by the Southold Historical Museum, with LF quoting the same passage; the newspaper itself was not read. The LF page is older: its grounds hours (daily 8 a.m. to dusk) and museum hours may be out of date; the museum's visitor page is used for hours. Wikipedia (Horton Point Light) was read for leads only and is not cited. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22: The story now states the disagreements LighthouseFriends raises that it had left out: nine head keepers (LF text) against eight (LF's own list and the archive); a 55-ft tower (LF) against 58 ft (museum); a fourth-order lens that LF says the museum displays, against the museum's statement that the third-order lens was lost; a 40-ft (LF) against 50-ft (museum) skeleton tower; a wartime Civilian Defense Corps (LF) against the military (museum). The 1860 traffic entry is quoted as printed; its listed figures add to 978, not 979. The 1933 Riverhead County Review passage is footnoted as quoted by the museum, because the paper itself was not read. LighthouseFriends' 'older page' remark was an unsupported claim (the page is undated) and was replaced by its visitor-hours statement, which differs from the museum's. The NRHP asset record's 'Date Published' (10/21/1994) is now given as the record date, not the listing date. COPYRIGHT PASS 2026-10-22: Quotations from copyrighted sources (LighthouseFriends, the museum site, the Times Union, the National Trust, HALPS) were reworded in the story; the remaining quoted text is the Light-House Board, Commissioner and keeper-log wording (public domain), one museum title, and short names. The evidence quotes in this file are internal and were left exact.
